what_this_is: The same seventeen rule classes and the same sampled items as the published screen, scored as a decision problem: efficacy (what obeying costs), necessity (what disobeying costs) and robustness (what the worst permitted move costs), in expected score as well as centipawns.
provenance_warning: THIS IS NOT THE PUBLISHED ENGINE. The published screen ran Stockfish 17.1 at 200,000 nodes; this run's build is recorded above. Every comparison in this file is therefore WITHIN this run -- b_valid is recomputed here by the published method so that the reordering is measured against a column produced by the same engine. No number here may be subtracted from a number in RULE_CLASS_SEARCH.md.

corpus.note: one record per (position, rule class that fired). A position can appear under several rule classes; they are different items and are never pooled.

RC-00.name: mate-in-one
RC-00.prescription: if a move mates, play it; a check that is not mate is the error

RC-01.name: loose-piece
RC-01.prescription: if exactly one enemy piece is capturable and undefended, take it

RC-02.name: recapture
RC-02.prescription: if the opponent just captured on a square you attack, take back there

RC-03.name: capture-the-checker
RC-03.prescription: when a single piece checks you and nothing defends it, capture it

RC-04.name: save-the-attacked-piece
RC-04.prescription: if exactly one of your pieces is attacked and materially threatened, move it

RC-05.name: safe-promotion
RC-05.prescription: if a pawn can promote to a square nothing attacks, promote

RC-06.name: answer-the-mate-threat
RC-06.prescription: if the opponent threatens mate next move, play a move that stops it

RC-07.name: answer-the-queen-threat
RC-07.prescription: if the opponent can win your queen, stop them

RC-08.name: answer-the-rook-threat
RC-08.prescription: if the opponent can win your rook, stop them

RC-09.name: answer-the-minor-threat
RC-09.prescription: if the opponent can win a knight or bishop, stop them

RC-11.name: move-the-threatened-minor
RC-11.prescription: if a knight or bishop of yours can be won, move it

RC-12.name: stop-the-promotion
RC-12.prescription: if the opponent can safely promote a pawn, prevent it

RC-13.name: underpromote-to-knight
RC-13.prescription: promote to a knight only when the knight gives check

RC-14.name: capture-the-mating-piece
RC-14.prescription: when one piece threatens mate next move, capture it

RC-18.name: move-the-piece-that-must-move
RC-18.prescription: if a minor of yours is attacked by something cheaper, move it

RC-20.name: defend-the-piece-in-place
RC-20.prescription: if a minor of yours hangs to an equal-or-dearer attacker, defend it where it stands

RC-21.name: push-the-unstoppable-passer
RC-21.prescription: if your passed pawn is outside the enemy king's square, push it

reordering.reading: A high rho means the decision model AGREES with the top-1 screen and the published ordering stands. A low rho means the published ordering is an artefact of measuring argmax agreement instead of value, and every design rule inferred from that ordering was inferred from the wrong column.
